Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates bilateral lung consolidation with multiple cystic lucencies (pseudocavitation) in the right midzone, a radiographic pattern highly characteristic of pneumonic-type lung adenocarcinoma (formerly bronchioloalveolar carcinoma). While tuberculosis and fungal infections can cause cavitation, the specific appearance of cystic spaces within extensive consolidation without typical upper lobe predominance or discrete nodules favors this malignancy.
